note: Authoritative delivery-wave assignment. Every status item appears exactly once; tools/backlog.py refuses missing, duplicate, unknown and reverse-wave dependency entries.
contract_note: Wave and release-profile objects define intended outcomes. Existing lint enforces item_waves and declared dependency order, not every semantic field or profile rule below. Until BK-80 is complete, apply a recorded manual release review; these objects confer no deployment approval.

wave_contracts.name: Trusted foundations
wave_contracts.goal: Make identity, storage, test controls and evidence claims dependable before they support privileged work.
entry_conditions: Existing product and corpus scope are inventoried; control populations and known limitations are explicit.
exit_conditions: Assigned foundation contracts pass their required controls; unresolved end-to-end integration is owned by later registered work.
BK-80 is complete before any automatically derived production claim relies on the new profile or evidence-validity rules.
wave_contracts.scope: Infrastructure and evidence foundations; synthetic or specifically authorised local use only.
wave_contracts.release_claim: Foundation conformance; no permission for a client pilot or production deployment.

wave_contracts.name: Admission and commission
wave_contracts.goal: Establish who instructs, what is being asked and whether the work may proceed.
entry_conditions: Relevant W0 foundations are proven; identity and workspace boundaries are established.
exit_conditions: Ordinary screening and narrow emergency integration pass separately; substantive work cannot bypass clearance.
Commission, professional role and authority remain visible and can be revised without silently widening scope.
wave_contracts.scope: Access, admission, task framing and authority.
wave_contracts.release_claim: Bounded admission conformance; substantive-quality claims await the relevant later waves.

wave_contracts.name: Usable file and interactive briefing
wave_contracts.goal: Make files recognisable and let advocates provide and refine the brief through typed, spoken and uploaded material.
entry_conditions: Admission foundation is available; media processing cannot precede BK-69 permission and quarantine boundaries.
exit_conditions: Intake retrieves authorised existing material, reflects understanding and asks purposeful questions with pause and return behavior.
BK-79 proves originals, derivatives, processing and deletion through the served path; current Phase A contracts pass at target widths.
wave_contracts.scope: Matter navigation/re-entry, research placement, evidence inventory and the briefing loop.
wave_contracts.release_claim: Usable-file and briefing conformance; intake completeness is task-specific, never a full merits assurance.

wave_contracts.name: Worked legal file
wave_contracts.goal: Connect the legal position to attributed facts, primary authority, alternatives, proof and useful relief.
entry_conditions: Current propositions and sources are available; governing legal and jurisdictional premises can be inspected.
exit_conditions: Changed material predicates invalidate affected conclusions while preserving unrelated work and prior versions.
Thresholds, adverse case, remedies and evidence gaps are assessed on representative matters with named legal-premise review.
wave_contracts.scope: Reasoning dependencies, thresholds, research, proof, case theory and expert evaluation foundation.
wave_contracts.release_claim: Worked-file conformance at a stated advice maturity; not authority to act.

wave_contracts.name: Considered advice
wave_contracts.goal: Produce practical, candid advice and a reliable decision experience.
entry_conditions: The task-specific file is ready for the claimed maturity; unsupported premises and production limitations remain visible.
exit_conditions: Options, proportionality, enforceability, adverse case and doing nothing are compared where relevant; decisions are recorded.
Latency, failure, cancellation and recovery are measured; expert review assesses actual served answers and user understanding.
wave_contracts.scope: Advice, decision support, progress and degraded-service behavior.
wave_contracts.release_claim: Advice conformance for the evaluated population and scope; no autonomous client or court action.

wave_contracts.name: Authorised action support
wave_contracts.goal: Prepare and verify drafts, negotiation, witness work and hearing assistance within recorded authority.
entry_conditions: Current advice, approved versions and professional-role authority are available.
exit_conditions: Every material draft assertion is traceable and every proposed external action requires the appropriate authority.
Filing, service and communications distinguish intention, transmission and verified outcome; uncertain delivery is reconciled before retry.
wave_contracts.scope: Drafting, filing control, negotiation and court preparation.
wave_contracts.release_claim: Conformance of the approved action workflow; activation of external integrations requires a separate deployment decision.

wave_contracts.name: Continuity and closure
wave_contracts.goal: Carry responsibility, decisions and obligations through change, handover and closure.
entry_conditions: Worked-file and action histories are current; recipient and continuing-service authority are known.
exit_conditions: Handover is current and acknowledged; remaining responsibilities do not disappear during transfer.
Events update obligations; closure is blocked until required deadlines, originals, funds, retention and authority issues are resolved or validly transferred.
wave_contracts.scope: Ongoing service, conflict watch, handover, event capture and closure.
wave_contracts.release_claim: Continuity and closure conformance for the tested workflow.

wave_contracts.name: Production release
wave_contracts.goal: Prove the deployed system can safely sustain the specifically approved service.
entry_conditions: The chosen release scope names required features, items, populations and reviewers; unresolved exclusions are approved and cannot silently remove critical safeguards.
exit_conditions: All production-profile conditions and applicable cumulative journeys pass on the deployed configuration; counsel review remains current.
MFA, tenant/access boundaries, capacity, monitoring, restore, rollback, accessibility and privacy outcomes are independently evidenced.
wave_contracts.scope: A named deployment, configured providers/corpus, authorised user population and operational support model.
wave_contracts.release_claim: Production approval only after a recorded accountable decision; a wave label or aggregate green count is not approval.

release_profiles.name: Controlled prototype
release_profiles.scope: Ordinary local development with synthetic data is not a release and does not wait for whole-product completion. A controlled demonstration activates only the named safe paths using synthetic or specifically authorised material.
entry_conditions: For an activated demonstration, name its environment, operator, material authority and exercised paths.
Local coding and synthetic unit tests may proceed against isolated components; do not present an incomplete exercised user route as conformant.
Confidential client material requires the pilot identity, security and processing gates, including BK-85 and BK-86, even if the session is called a demonstration.
required_evidence: Current local controls for every exercised path
Human inspection of known limitations and data authority
excluded_claims: Phase A completion before all Phase A contracts and served proof pass
Considered legal advice merely because a demonstration returns an answer
Permission to process real client material without explicit authority
release_profiles.approval: This is a scope definition, not approval to run a demonstration or use client data. Record the accountable authorisation for the intended use.

conditional_items.when: the demonstration exercises registration, recovery or privileged matter access
any confidential client material is admitted, including a demonstration
adaptive lead investigation or advice is enabled in the declared scope
specialist delegation or delegated document generation is enabled in the declared scope

release_profiles.name: Bounded advocate pilot
release_profiles.scope: A named invited advocate population, authorised materials, declared corpus/jurisdiction and enabled feature set; supervised decisions and no undeclared external action.
entry_conditions: Publish the exact enabled user journeys, supported media/languages and remaining limitations.
Name qualified reviewers, stop conditions, incident owner and the expiry/review date of pilot approval.

conditional_items.when: any spoken, uploaded or mixed-media material is enabled
drafting, filing or negotiation is enabled
adaptive lead investigation or advice is enabled in the declared scope
specialist delegation or delegated document generation is enabled in the declared scope

required_evidence: Current served journey for enabled scope with expected populations
Current representative-matter model evaluation and qualified counsel review
Environment-specific security, privacy and recovery review
excluded_claims: Support for untested courts, languages, media or external actions
Automatic waiver of MFA or other material security requirements
release_profiles.approval: Pilot activation requires an explicit accountable, bounded approval naming material risks and compensating controls. No prototype decision or this plan grants it.

release_profiles.name: Named production release
release_profiles.scope: A specific deployment and release manifest defining users, tenancy, legal coverage, enabled features, processing, service levels and operating responsibilities.
entry_conditions: Publish the exact release manifest and all applicable pilot and production obligations.
Obtain a current qualified legal review of relied-on governing premises and professional-role restrictions.

conditional_items.when: adaptive lead investigation or advice is enabled in the declared scope
specialist delegation or delegated document generation is enabled in the declared scope

required_evidence: Current complete automated and served proof for the release manifest
Measured security, restore, rollback, accessibility, capacity and service outcomes on the deployment shape
excluded_claims: Approval inferred from row counts, a test-only PASS or a generated workbook
release_profiles.approval: No release is authorised by this plan. Accountable production sign-off is required; any material exception must be separately approved, owned, expiring and visible with compensating controls. D-013 does not grant a production MFA exception.

journey_model.principle: The 47 steps are observable obligations, not 47 mandatory screens. Take the Brief, Work the File and Advise share one current file and can loop.
normal_loop: Ask the smallest useful question or material request
Work the file and advise at permitted maturity
return_triggers: new material fact or conflicting source
new party, event, deadline or legal premise
advocate correction, disagreement or new task
journey_model.return_behavior: Invalidate affected conclusions, clearance and readiness; preserve unchanged work and history; explain the change and return to the earliest necessary assessment, not the start of a fixed questionnaire.
journey_model.stop_and_resume: Stop or pause when the task is answered at permitted maturity, material is unavailable, the advocate elects to pause, authority is missing or a justified refusal applies. Record the gap, consequence, owner and resume trigger; do not keep asking solely to fill empty fields.
journey_model.maturity: AM-01 to AM-05 are permissions for a particular output, not a confidence score or a one-way progress bar. New facts may downgrade readiness; action authority remains separate from advice quality.
